title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.9113: kappa = 1.0002 from a 512-table hazard census on 87fa94f0

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.9113 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on this solver's 87fa94f0 (125.9139) and changes only kappa, from 1.002 to 1.0002; the counted loops (pass 1 unrolled 128 times, pass 2 16 times), the arrival rows, the ordinary step of 578.578125 + 25112/2^20 = 578.6021 instructions, h = 0.000203 and p0 = 0.3902033 are unchanged. kappa = 1.0002 rests on the shipped hazard census at checkpoint period 256: with the production waste w <= 2^-14.56, (1 + w)(kappa_eff + 2 s.e.) is 1.00008 for its 512-table walk run at q29, R = 2^20, dp_bits 5 (kappa_eff = 0.99976 +- 0.00014) and 1.00015 for the seven walk runs pooled (kappa_eff = 0.999884 +- 0.000111, chi^2 = 6.0 on 6); no walk run's (1 + w)kappa_eff exceeds 1.0002 by one standard error; the 512-table ideal-mapping control gives rho = 0.99976 +- 0.00028; the tc runs' walk values lie within 1.5 standard errors of 1.0002. Rare exits charge 20 milli-units each and run the inline kernel's own instructions; the declared run enters all 383 exit stubs. Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39 (failure rows 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.0002*S0 = 2^126.7000183, phase 1 = 2^125.910662, hard extras = 2^112.575681, allowance = 2^114.3813, W_ledger = 2^125.9112892 < 2^125.9113; Markov ratio 0.000198611 (experiment.py's float ledger: 0.000198616) < 0.000203; certificate.py checks W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1259113 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1259112 exactly. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail anchor phases) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7, with node routing and a long-trail trap test; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped unrolled loops (with their rare exits, on constructed inputs that enter every stub), emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger of proof.md recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
